detailedExplanation: Verified against The Tiffin Girls’ School Year 9 Chemistry Curriculum Outline 2026–27 (AQA GCSE Chemistry 8462).
Collision theory states that reacting particles must collide, and collisions must have enough energy for a reaction to occur. The rate depends on how frequently successful collisions happen.
Increasing concentration or gas pressure places more particles in a given volume, increasing collision frequency. Increasing surface area exposes more particles to collision.
Increasing temperature makes particles move faster, increasing collision frequency and increasing the fraction of collisions with energy at least equal to the activation energy.
A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy. It speeds up the reaction without being used up overall.

additionalSourceSections.heading: Rate
additionalSourceSections.body:
Rate = amount of reactant used or product formed ÷ time
Faster rate when successful collisions happen more often.
↑ concentration / ↑ gas pressure / ↑ surface area → more frequent collisions
↑ temperature → particles move faster + larger fraction exceed activation energy
Catalyst → lower activation energy pathway.
